4. Backtest¶

  • This notebook simulates trading strategies based on model outputs from predictions.csv, evaluated over the May 2017 – December 2024 test period.
  • Two strategy types are tested for each of the 7 models (RF-252, RF-504, XGB-252, XGB-504, LGB-252, LGB-504, and the Ensemble): long-flat (long on predicted UP days, flat otherwise) and long-short (long on predicted UP days, short on predicted DOWN days).
  • Transaction costs are modelled as the sum of commission, spread, and slippage, applied on every position change. The size of the change determines the cost: entering or exiting a position costs 1×, reversing from long to short (or vice versa) costs 2×.
  • Realistic transaction costs are modelled as 3 basis points per trade (1 bp each for commission, bid-ask spread, and slippage), consistent with typical costs of trading a liquid ETF such as SPY.
  • Each strategy is evaluated against a buy-and-hold SPY benchmark using: annualised return, annualised volatility, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and average drawdown.
  • Sharpe ratio is computed using the 10-Year Treasury yield (DGS10) as the risk-free rate.
  • The backtest is run under two cost scenarios — zero costs and realistic costs.

Setup¶

# Loading DGS10 risk-free rate (10-Year Treasury)
dgs10 = pd.read_csv("../Data/dgs10.csv", index_col="observation_date", parse_dates=True)
dgs10 = dgs10["DGS10"].ffill() / 100 / 252  # convert to daily rate

Backtest function¶

def backtest(predictions, pred_col, mode, commission=0, spread=0, slippage=0):

    df = predictions[["spy_return"]].copy()

    if mode == "long_flat":
        df["signal"] = predictions[pred_col].map({1: 1, 0: 0})
    else:
        df["signal"] = predictions[pred_col].map({1: 1, 0: -1})

    position_change = (df["signal"] - df["signal"].shift(1)).abs()
    position_change.iloc[0] = 0
    total_cost = commission + spread + slippage
    df["net_return"]   = df["signal"] * df["spy_return"] - position_change * total_cost
    df["equity_strat"] = (1 + df["net_return"]).cumprod()
    df["equity_bnh"]   = (1 + df["spy_return"]).cumprod()

    def _metrics(returns, label):
        rf_daily = dgs10.reindex(returns.index).ffill()
        excess   = returns - rf_daily
        n        = len(returns)
        total    = (1 + returns).prod() - 1
        ann_ret  = (1 + total) ** (252 / n) - 1
        ann_vol  = returns.std() * np.sqrt(252)
        sharpe   = excess.mean() / excess.std() * np.sqrt(252)
        equity   = (1 + returns).cumprod()
        dd       = (equity - equity.cummax()) / equity.cummax()
        return {
            "total_return":   round(total, 4),
            "ann_return":     round(ann_ret, 4),
            "ann_volatility": round(ann_vol, 4),
            "sharpe":         round(sharpe, 4),
            "max_drawdown":   round(dd.min(), 4),
            "avg_drawdown":   round(dd[dd < 0].mean(), 4),
            "strategy/model": label,
        }

    metrics = pd.DataFrame([
        _metrics(df["spy_return"], "Buy & Hold"),
        _metrics(df["net_return"], pred_col),
    ]).set_index("strategy/model")

    return metrics, df

Costs setup¶

# Zero costs
costs_zero = dict(commission=0.0000, spread=0.0000, slippage=0.0000)

# Realistic costs
costs_real = dict(commission=0.0001, spread=0.0001, slippage=0.0001)

# Backtest run
models = {
    "Random walk": "rw",
    "RF-252":      "rf252",
    "RF-504":      "rf504",
    "XGB-252":     "xgb252",
    "XGB-504":     "xgb504",
    "LGB-252":     "lgb252",
    "LGB-504":     "lgb504",
    "Ensemble":    "ensemble",
}

results = {}

for scenario_name, costs in [("Zero costs", costs_zero), ("Realistic costs", costs_real)]:
    rows_lf, equity_lf = [], {}
    rows_ls, equity_ls = [], {}

    for label, pred_col in models.items():
        m_lf, df_lf = backtest(predictions=predictions, pred_col=pred_col, mode="long_flat",  **costs)
        m_ls, df_ls = backtest(predictions=predictions, pred_col=pred_col, mode="long_short", **costs)
        rows_lf.append(m_lf.loc[pred_col].rename(label))
        rows_ls.append(m_ls.loc[pred_col].rename(label))
        equity_lf[label] = df_lf["equity_strat"]
        equity_ls[label] = df_ls["equity_strat"]

    bnh_equity = df_lf["equity_bnh"]
    bnh_row    = m_lf.loc["Buy & Hold"].rename("Buy & Hold")

    results[scenario_name] = {
        "lf":        pd.concat([bnh_row.to_frame().T, pd.DataFrame(rows_lf)]),
        "ls":        pd.concat([bnh_row.to_frame().T, pd.DataFrame(rows_ls)]),
        "equity_lf": equity_lf,
        "equity_ls": equity_ls,
    }

bnh_equity_global = bnh_equity

for scenario_name, res in results.items():
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Scenario: {scenario_name}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print("Long-Flat:")
    display(res["lf"])
    print("Long-Short:")
    display(res["ls"])

# Yearly breakdown of the ensemble model performance
yearly_rows = []

for scenario_name, res in results.items():
    ens_equity = res["equity_lf"]["Ensemble"]
    for year, grp in ens_equity.groupby(ens_equity.index.year):
        ann_ret = grp.iloc[-1] / grp.iloc[0] - 1
        yearly_rows.append({"year": year, "strategy": f"Ensemble ({scenario_name})", "ann_return": round(ann_ret, 4)})

for year, grp in bnh_equity_global.groupby(bnh_equity_global.index.year):
    ann_ret = grp.iloc[-1] / grp.iloc[0] - 1
    yearly_rows.append({"year": year, "strategy": "Buy & Hold", "ann_return": round(ann_ret, 4)})

yearly_df = pd.DataFrame(yearly_rows)

# Yearly breakdown visualized
years     = sorted(yearly_df["year"].unique())
x         = np.arange(len(years))
width     = 0.25

bnh_vals  = yearly_df[yearly_df["strategy"] == "Buy & Hold"].set_index("year")["ann_return"]
zero_vals = yearly_df[yearly_df["strategy"] == "Ensemble (Zero costs)"].set_index("year")["ann_return"]
real_vals = yearly_df[yearly_df["strategy"] == "Ensemble (Realistic costs)"].set_index("year")["ann_return"]

with plt.style.context("ggplot"):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 7))

    bars_bnh  = ax.bar(x - width, [bnh_vals[y]  for y in years], width, label="Buy & Hold",                 color="#E8856A")
    bars_zero = ax.bar(x,         [zero_vals[y] for y in years], width, label="Ensemble (Zero costs)",      color="#3DBDC4")
    bars_real = ax.bar(x + width, [real_vals[y] for y in years], width, label="Ensemble (Realistic costs)", color="#5A9BD5")

    for bars in [bars_bnh, bars_zero, bars_real]:
        for bar in bars:
            v = bar.get_height()
            ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
                    v + (0.002 if v >= 0 else -0.006),
                    f"{v:.1%}", ha="center", va="bottom" if v >= 0 else "top",
                    fontsize=8, color="#000000")

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(years)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.set_title("Annual returns — Ensemble (both scenarios) vs Buy & Hold (Long-Flat)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Annual return")
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
    ax.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Ensemble vs Benchmark comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 7))

for ax, scenario_name in zip(axes, ["Zero costs", "Realistic costs"]):
    ens_eq = results[scenario_name]["equity_lf"]["Ensemble"]
    bnh_eq = bnh_equity_global

    bnh_eq.plot(ax=ax, color="black",   linewidth=1.5, label="Buy & Hold", zorder=3)
    ens_eq.plot(ax=ax, color="#3DBDC4", linewidth=1.5, label="Ensemble",   zorder=3)

    years = sorted(ens_eq.index.year.unique())
    for i, year in enumerate(years):
        mask = ens_eq.index.year == year
        x0, x1 = ens_eq.index[mask][0], ens_eq.index[mask][-1]
        if i % 2 == 0:
            ax.axvspan(x0, x1, color="lightgrey", alpha=0.3, zorder=0)

    ax.fill_between(ens_eq.index, ens_eq, bnh_eq,
                    where=ens_eq >= bnh_eq, interpolate=True,
                    color="#3DBDC4", alpha=0.3, label="Ensemble ahead")
    ax.fill_between(ens_eq.index, ens_eq, bnh_eq,
                    where=ens_eq <  bnh_eq, interpolate=True,
                    color="#E8856A", alpha=0.3, label="Buy & Hold ahead")

    ymin = ax.get_ylim()[0]
    for year in years:
        mask = ens_eq.index.year == year
        x0, x1 = ens_eq.index[mask][0], ens_eq.index[mask][-1]
        ax.text(x0 + (x1 - x0) / 2, ymin, str(year),
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8, color="grey")

    ax.set_title(f"Equity — Ensemble vs Buy & Hold (Long-Flat, {scenario_name})")
    ax.set_ylabel("Equity")
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.legend()
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Summary¶

Zero transaction costs¶

  • The long-flat Ensemble returns 12.22% annualised, nearly matching buy-and-hold (12.44%), with a better Sharpe ratio (0.68 vs 0.58) and lower max drawdown (−26.5% vs −34.1%).
  • Best individual model: XGB-252 (long-flat) — Sharpe 0.67, annualised return 11.73%.
  • Long-short strategies underperform long-flat across all models.

Realistic transaction costs¶

  • Costs significantly erode performance.
  • The long-flat Ensemble drops to 9.27% annualised (Sharpe: 0.50).
  • All models fall below the buy-and-hold benchmark.
  • Long-short strategies are unsustainable — each reversal doubles the cost. The Ensemble reaches only 4.75% annualised.

Best performer: Ensemble (long-flat)¶

  • Zero costs: 12.22% annualised, Sharpe 0.68 — 0.22 pp below buy-and-hold in return, but better risk-adjusted performance and lower max drawdown (−26.5% vs −34.1%).
  • Realistic costs: 9.27% annualised, Sharpe 0.50 — no longer beats buy-and-hold in return or on a risk-adjusted basis, though max drawdown remains lower (−28.2% vs −34.1%).
